qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Jonas Sjöstedt (The Left) Subject:

In its resolution of 30 April 2026 on the new Chinese law on ‘ethnic unity and progress’ and the intensified suppression of ethnic identities1, Parliament called for sanctions on individuals and entities in charge of conceiving and implementing the Chinese ‘Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress’ (or ‘Ethnic Unity Law’) under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, owing to the law’s extraterritorial effects and the intensification of the forceful assimilation of ethnic groups in China. Given that the Ethnic Unity Law came into force on 1 July 2026 without changes, what are the next steps the European External Action Service is taking to ensure that sanctions are imposed as requested by Parliament?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.11.2026) The EU’s position on the human rights and rule of law situation in China is well known and has been set out in its public statements and in its exchanges with the Chinese authorities, including in the framework of the EU-China Human Rights Dialogue1 and in statements at the UN Human Rights Council2. The EU has expressed its concerns about the human rights situation in China and has repeatedly urged China to abide by its obligations under national and international law, to respect, protect and fulfil human rights for all, and to uphold the rule of law. These concerns include the situation in Xinjiang, Tibetan areas and Hong Kong, as well as the situation of human rights defenders, lawyers and journalists. The EU has repeatedly called on China to respect the rights of persons belonging to ethnic, religious and linguistic minorities, including their right to freely enjoy and preserve their culture, religion or belief, language and identity. The EU will continue to engage with China on human rights and the rule of law, both bilaterally and in multilateral fora, while reiterating its long-standing position that respect for human rights, fundamental freedoms, due process and the rule of law are essential elements of EUChina relations. Any decision to list natural or legal persons under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime is to be taken by the 27 Member States of the Council. When exercising the right of initiative, the High Representative/Vice-President (HR/VP) will take all political considerations into account. The ultimate decision on any proposals, made by the HR/VP or one or more Member States, lies with the Council. The discussions and deliberations in the Council leading up to any such decision are confidential and cannot be commented on.
